segments.t: Inside the Hamburg supermarket Feinkost Kolinski, deputy manager Pina updates branch boss Thorsten on the fruit order before the weekend rush. Just as she brings up last week's delivery trouble, the office phone interrupts them. Listen to the German conversation first without worrying about catching every detail.
Ich halte dich kurz auf dem Laufenden, was wir bestellt haben.
Wir haben Erdbeeren und Bananen bestellt.
Das Wochenende kommt, und die Leute gehen an den Strand.
Wollen wir bei den Wassermelonen die doppelte Menge bestellen?
Eigentlich geht doch Kernobst gerade gut.
Nee, eigentlich gerade nicht so, das haben wir letzte Woche gesehen.
Da haben wir nur die Hälfte verkauft.
Übrigens gab es letzte Woche ein bisschen Lieferprobleme.
Kruse am Apparat!
Let's walk through Pina's fruit order and see how workplace updates and polite suggestions sound in everyday German.
Ich halte dich kurz auf dem Laufenden, was wir bestellt haben.

'Let me quickly keep you posted on what we ordered.' Pina opens with a lively workplace idiom that literally pictures holding someone on the running track so they stay up to speed. Adding the little word for briefly makes the update sound brisk and considerate.
Wir haben Erdbeeren und Bananen bestellt.

'We ordered strawberries and bananas.' Notice how German wraps the past action around the middle of the sentence: the helper comes second, while the word for ordered waits right at the end. Both fruit names are transparent compounds or international cousins that are easy to spot.
Das Wochenende kommt, und die Leute gehen an den Strand.

'The weekend is coming, and people are going to the beach.' The word for weekend joins week and end into one neat block, just like English. At the close, going to the beach uses the preposition for onto the edge of the water rather than the plain word for to.
Wollen wir bei den Wassermelonen die doppelte Menge bestellen?

'Shall we order double the amount of watermelons?' Starting a question with this modal action word is the everyday way to say 'shall we' when making a team suggestion. The word for watermelons is built word for word from water and melons, and the final action word again lands cleanly at the end.
Eigentlich geht doch Kernobst gerade gut.

'Actually, pome fruit is selling well right now, isn't it?' Thorsten reaches for a supermarket trade compound meaning seeded orchard fruit like apples and pears. Notice how the everyday verb for 'goes' doubles here as 'sells', while the little middle particle nudges Pina to agree.
Nee, eigentlich gerade nicht so, das haben wir letzte Woche gesehen.

'Nah, not really right now — we saw that last week.' That casual northern word for 'nah' is softer and more relaxed than a textbook 'no' among coworkers. She softens her pushback further with a handy chunk meaning 'not really right now' before backing it up with last week's results.
Übrigens gab es letzte Woche ein bisschen Lieferprobleme.

'By the way, there were some delivery problems last week.' The opening transition word is what you can say whenever a side topic pops into your head. Because it takes the first slot, 'there was' flips its order right behind it, leading into the compound word for delivery problems.
Kruse am Apparat!

'Kruse speaking!' On a German landline, people often give their surname followed by 'at the apparatus' — meaning at the telephone set. Swap in your own last name and you have a classic, slightly old-school way to pick up an office phone. Now let's hear the whole office exchange again from start to finish.
Ich halte dich kurz auf dem Laufenden, was wir bestellt haben.
Wir haben Erdbeeren und Bananen bestellt.
Das Wochenende kommt, und die Leute gehen an den Strand.
Wollen wir bei den Wassermelonen die doppelte Menge bestellen?
Eigentlich geht doch Kernobst gerade gut.
Nee, eigentlich gerade nicht so, das haben wir letzte Woche gesehen.
Da haben wir nur die Hälfte verkauft.
Übrigens gab es letzte Woche ein bisschen Lieferprobleme.
Kruse am Apparat!

Thorsten grabs the ringing phone before Pina can finish explaining the delivery mix-up. You now have handy ways to update a colleague, suggest a bigger order for the weekend, talk about half of something selling, and answer a work phone. See you next time!
Bis später!
